order: The chunk spans two sheets, so each sheet has its own .more file holding its one roster article: mittelrhein on germany, virginia on new-york.
check: check-fragment reports one problem per file and nothing else: regions[0].deeper is required for an article off the map. This edition writes no deeper list (the task's rule, as in c1 to c4), so the integrator relaxes that .more rule; with only that rule relaxed both files pass whole, with no superlative note. Not deepened, each article is held to the one prose total (800 to 1,800 words, every place note counted), 6 to 14 cards and 6 to 12 questions with at least 3 multiple choice. No key is the longest option. An apply-roster --dry run over a copy of the fragments with both files added reports no clash and would set germany's regionsOrder to end in mittelrhein and new-york's to end in virginia.
cms: germany (the Court's pages 47 to 51) writes a Certified row for the Mittelrhein: steep slopes along the Rhein, continental climate, Riesling as the main grape, slate soil; all four are in the summary, terroir, an exam line, a card and a question each. The Germany rows that a Mittelrhein label carries are applied in place: the Rhine as the moderating, light-reflecting river and the uplands as shelter, steep south-facing slopes, Fuder and Stück or steel, residual sugar against acidity, chaptalisation allowed for Qualitätswein and not for Prädikatswein, Deutscher Sekt and Sekt b.A., the Prädikat ladder by ripeness at harvest, the VDP with the Grosses Gewächs and Erstes Gewächs, Einzellage and the village with -er, trocken, halbtrocken and feinherb, Schloss on a label, the 1971 law and the service and pairing of dry and off dry Riesling. new-york (page 60) writes no row for Virginia and no CMS subject names it; the Codex's Régionale bank asks Virginia for Viognier and Cabernet Franc, humidity over cold and Jefferson's failure at Monticello, and the Village bank asks the two Shenandoah Valley AVAs; all of these are covered untagged, so asked starts at intro. The Mittelrhein's asked starts at certified, since the Court's Introductory rows name only the Mosel, Pfalz, Rheinhessen and Rheingau.
aliases: Every roster alias is claimed. Added for Mittelrhein: lorelei, bereich loreley, bopparder hamm, boppard hamm, bacharacher hahn, bacharacher wolfshohle, steeg, steeger st jost, kaub, st goarshausen, st goar, engeholl, oberweseler oelsberg, leutesdorf, siebengebirge, bereich siebengebirge, konigswinter, koenigswinter, drachenfels. Lorch stays the Rheingau's. Added for Virginia: monticello ava, charlottesville, northern virginia, northern neck, virginia s eastern shore, virginias eastern shore, rocky knob, north fork of roanoke, appalachian high country. Not claimed: northern neck george washington birthplace, which the join refuses because it holds the sheet word washington (northern neck stands in for it), and the bare shenandoah valley, which california.json sends to the california country key; Virginia's AVA holds that bare name in law, so the integrator may wish to point it at virginia or leave it as it is.

articles.name: Mittelrhein
uncertain: The two Bereiche, Loreley and Siebengebirge, rest on wein.plus and the regional summaries; the older Bereich names (Bacharach, Rheinburgengau) were not confirmed and are left out. Bereich Loreley is written as every vineyard in Rhineland-Palatinate because the Siebengebirge is the North Rhine-Westphalia part; the boundary was not read in the law.

The Grosslage name Petersberg for the Siebengebirge rests on one source (wein.plus); the count of Grosslagen (eleven in one source) and Einzellagen (111) is left out, as are the hectares (439 for 2025 in one source, 460 to 466 in others).
Riesling as about two thirds of the vineyard rests on figures of 64 to 70 per cent across three sources; Spätburgunder as about a tenth on one (10.3 per cent). No exact share is given.

Only the Hahn (the VDP's own page, inclined at 65 to 70 per cent) and the Wolfshöhle (the regional wine body) are named as VDP Grosse Lagen; the St. Jost, the Oelsberg, the Engehöll and the Bopparder Hamm sites are written as sites, with no classification claimed.
The Bopparder Hamm's Mandelstein and Ohlenberg are named from standard knowledge beside the Feuerlay, which a listing confirms; the Hamm's size (75 hectares in one source) is left out.
Heylesen Werth as an island vineyard at Bacharach rests on wein.plus's site list alone, and the vines on the lower slopes of the Drachenfels rest on standard knowledge; both are tagged master.

The UNESCO inscription of 29 June 2002 and the 65 kilometres from Bingen and Rüdesheim to Koblenz rest on the UNESCO nomination file and site page. The region's own length is written as over 100 kilometres, the river distance from Bingen to the Siebengebirge, since sources give 110 or 120.
The Lorelei at about 130 metres rests on one source (132 metres); the legend is written as Romantic poetry with no poet or date.

One of the smallest of the thirteen is kept as a measured statement (the Codex's own Court row says the same of the Ahr, and the Mittelrhein and the Hessische Bergstrasse are close in area); no rank is claimed.

No Mittelrhein amendment from 2020 to 2026 was found beyond the federal law of January 2021 (the Grosslage to carry Region, Grosses and Erstes Gewächs as legal terms) and an amendment of the protected designation's specification dated 19 October 2023 on analytical characteristics, whose text was not read and is not cited.

Producers whose trading name is a living person's full name are left out (several of the region's leading estates); Toni Jost is left out too, since it was not settled whether the person in the name is living.

articles.name: Virginia
uncertain: The law changes of the period: Virginia Peninsula was established by the final rule of 25 August 2021, effective 24 September 2021 (the Federal Register and the petitioning winery agree); Middleburg Virginia by the final rule of 13 September 2012. A proposed expansion of the Monticello AVA (2018) was found, but whether it was made final was not, so no size is given. TTB lists pending petitions; none in Virginia was confirmed, and the AVA list is undated rather than counted.

The founding dates of Monticello (1984 by memory), the Shenandoah Valley, the Northern Neck George Washington Birthplace, Virginia's Eastern Shore, Rocky Knob, the North Fork of Roanoke and the Appalachian High Country were not confirmed and are left out; a 1987 boundary revision of Monticello was seen, not used.
Viognier's 2011 title is written as the Virginia Wine Board's signature grape and a marketing choice, since sources disagree on whether it was ever an official state grape.

No planting ranking is given: the Virginia grape report was not found, so Chardonnay is written as planted widely and Cabernet Franc as the red that copes, with no claim of first place. The claim that Virginia holds the second planting of Petit Manseng after Jurançon rests on one guide and is left out.
Acte 12 of 1619 rests on the printed laws of the first General Assembly (ten vines a year for every householder); some secondary sources say twelve or twenty, which the article does not follow.

Norton raised in Richmond in the 1820s rests on several summaries with dates from 1817 to 1830 and on Wine Grapes; the parentage of Norton is not claimed. Norton as the same variety as Cynthiana rests on Wine Grapes.

Jefferson and Mazzei in the 1770s rests on several sources that differ on the land; the article says only that Mazzei planted beside Monticello and that the vines failed. Jefferson Vineyards on Mazzei's land rests on two secondary sources.

Barboursville's founding in 1976 by a Veneto family rests on WineAmerica and standard knowledge; the family is not named, as some of its members are living. Horton's founding year (1983 in one source) and the state's Farm Winery Act date (1980 or 1971, sources conflict) are left out.
Pierce's disease in the warm south-east, the Shenandoah Valley as drier than the Piedmont, and Chrysalis's devotion to Norton and Albariño rest on standard knowledge, not on a search.
Producers are named by trading name only; Linden, Horton, Boxwood and Chrysalis are not dated, and no founder is named.
